title: Accept the cap report from a file
action: Per D12 (issue 102). A host worktree guard refuses shell arguments that contain the word bash, and the cap proof must equal a cell verify that runs bash, so the --report JSON cannot be passed. In verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs add `report-file` to CAP_FLAGS and FINISH_FLAGS (bump the array lengths) and, where the flags are parsed (`let report = opt_string_flag(flags, "report")?;`), read the file at that path (relative to the cwd) as the raw report string when `--report-file` is given; giving both `--report` and `--report-file` refuses with `--report and --report-file are exclusive`; an unreadable file refuses naming the path. Validation stays in the existing report parser. The flag text is hand-declared in generated/registry_payload.json (catalog.rs reads REGISTRY_PAYLOAD and declares no flags): add `report-file` to the cells cap and cells finish entries there by hand, following the `deviations-file` entry. `report-file` is a new distinct flag name, so bump `PINNED_FLAG_COUNT` in catalog.rs by one (227 to 228 at plan time — read the current value) with a reason line in the same style as the earlier bumps there (that pin comment is the one comment this cell may add, as the existing bumps do). Red first: in verbs/cells/tests.rs add a test that caps a claimed cell with --report-file holding a valid report and asserts trace.report matches, and one that both flags refuse. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.
